For its official forms, see Hindi and Urdu. | The word *Hindustani* in the Devanagari and the Nastaliq-style Perso-Arabic scripts |. | Official language in | * India  (as Hindi and Urdu) * Pakistan   (as Urdu) * Fiji  (as Fijian Hindustani)  |. **Hindustani** is an Indo-Aryan language spoken in North India and Pakistan as the lingua franca of the region. Hindustani is a pluricentric language with two standard registers "Register (sociolinguistics)"), known as Hindi (Prakritised and Sanskritised "Sanskritisation (linguistics)") register written in the Brahmic script) and Urdu (Persianised and Arabised register written in the Perso-Arabic script), which serve as official languages of India and Pakistan, respectively. The concept of a Hindustani language as a "unifying language" or "fusion language" that could transcend communal and religious divisions across the subcontinent was endorsed by Mahatma Gandhi, as it was not seen to be associated with either the Hindu or Muslim communities as was the case with Hindi and Urdu respectively, and it was also considered a simpler language for people to learn.
